questions.question: If you must drive in reverse, what should you do?

options.text: Drive as fast as possible to finish quickly.
Get out and walk around to check for obstacles first.
Use only the passenger side mirror.
Stick your head out the window to look backward.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get out and walk around to check for obstacles first.
questions.explanation: Walk around your vehicle to check for hazards before backing up. Use both side mirrors while backing. Always back up slowly.

questions.question: Heavy steering often means:

options.text: A rear tire has failed.
A front tire has failed.
The load has shifted.
The coolant is overheating.

questions.correctAnswerText: A front tire has failed.
questions.explanation: Heavy steering usually means a front tire has failed. If your steering feels different, pull off the road safely and check your tires.

questions.question: What is the smallest allowed size for a hazmat placard?

options.text: Four square inches
Seven square inches
10 ¾ square inches
32 square inches

questions.correctAnswerText: 10 ¾ square inches
questions.explanation: Hazmat placards must be diamond-shaped and at least 10 ¾ square inches.

questions.question: What does the suspension system do?

options.text: Supports the vehicle and its load.
Keeps the load the proper distance from the driver's area.
Maintains safe distance between vehicles.
Reduces weight on the tires.

questions.correctAnswerText: Supports the vehicle and its load.
questions.explanation: The suspension system supports a vehicle and its load while keeping the axles in place. A damaged suspension system is very dangerous.

questions.question: The drive shaft should be:

options.text: Bent toward the passenger side.
Bent toward the driver side.
Bent to one side or the other.
Straight with no bending.

questions.correctAnswerText: Straight with no bending.
questions.explanation: During a vehicle inspection, check that the drive shaft is not bent or cracked.

questions.question: What is a standee line?

options.text: A line on the bus floor showing where passengers cannot stand.
A single-file line of standing passengers.
A mark showing the maximum number of people on a bus.
A mark showing the maximum height of passengers.

questions.correctAnswerText: A line on the bus floor showing where passengers cannot stand.
questions.explanation: While a bus is moving, standing passengers cannot go past the rear of the driver's seat. A two-inch line on the floor marks this boundary. This is called the standee line.

questions.question: If a vehicle has an inspection report, the driver should:

options.text: Ignore the report and find issues themselves.
Take the vehicle to a mechanic.
Read the report.
Skip the pre-trip inspection and only use the report.

questions.correctAnswerText: Read the report.
questions.explanation: Start your inspection by reading the last inspection report. The carrier should have fixed any problems listed on it.

questions.question: A convex mirror is sometimes called a ____ mirror.

options.text: Bug-eye
Square
Helper

questions.correctAnswerText: Bug-eye
questions.explanation: Large vehicles often have curved, convex mirrors called "fisheye," "spot," or "bug-eye" mirrors. They show a wider view than flat mirrors but make objects look smaller and farther away than they really are.

questions.question: When checking your vehicle before driving, look under it to see:

options.text: If the vehicle is on an incline.
If there are fresh fluid leaks under the vehicle.
If the vehicle is in a parking spot.
If the vehicle is on a decline.

questions.correctAnswerText: If there are fresh fluid leaks under the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Look under your vehicle for fresh oil, coolant, grease, or fuel leaks. Leaks can mean the vehicle has unsafe problems.

questions.question: What affects a vehicle's height?

options.text: Color
Length
Weight
Number of windows

questions.correctAnswerText: Weight
questions.explanation: A heavy load makes a vehicle sit lower. A light load makes it sit higher. If your full vehicle fits under a bridge, an empty vehicle may be taller and not fit.

questions.question: When stopping a manual transmission vehicle, what should you do as the engine slows down?

options.text: Push in the clutch.
Push out the clutch.
Shift into neutral.
Shut off the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Push in the clutch.
questions.explanation: Push in the clutch when stopping a manual transmission vehicle as the engine slows down.

questions.question: What is a danger of looking at one mirror for too long?

options.text: You will be distracted by potential hazards.
You may not see a hazard ahead of you.
The mirrors may shake and move.
You may notice a dirty spot on the mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may not see a hazard ahead of you.
questions.explanation: Look at mirrors quickly. If you look at one mirror too long, you may travel far without seeing what is ahead. You could miss important hazards.

questions.question: Can gasoline be brought onto a bus?

options.text: Yes, gasoline can be brought onto a bus.
No, gasoline can never be brought onto a bus.
Yes, gasoline can be stored in the passenger area during long trips.
Yes, if stored in glass containers.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, gasoline can never be brought onto a bus.
questions.explanation: Gasoline and other hazardous items are not allowed on buses. Bus drivers and passengers must not bring gasoline or car batteries onto a bus.

questions.question: In an emergency, if you must drive onto the shoulder, what should you do?

options.text: Brake as hard as possible.
Keep all wheels on the shoulder.
Stop safely on the shoulder before returning to the road.
Stay on the shoulder until the next exit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop safely on the shoulder before returning to the road.
questions.explanation: Keep one set of wheels on the pavement to stay in control. Stop completely on the shoulder if possible. Then return to the road when it is safe.

questions.question: What do move over laws require?

options.text: Trucks to use the left lane.
All vehicles to leave the lane next to a stopped emergency vehicle with flashing lights.
All vehicles to use the left lane.
All vehicles to move to the left lane if a flatbed trailer is in the right lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: All vehicles to leave the lane next to a stopped emergency vehicle with flashing lights.
questions.explanation: Move over laws require drivers to leave the lane next to a stopped emergency vehicle with lights flashing. If you cannot move over safely, slow down and drive with caution.

questions.question: What should happen if a bus breaks down with passengers still on board?

options.text: Another bus should push it to the destination.
The bus should be towed to its destination.
Passengers should push the bus.
The bus should be towed to the nearest safe place to let passengers off.

questions.correctAnswerText: The bus should be towed to the nearest safe place to let passengers off.
questions.explanation: Do not tow or push a disabled bus unless absolutely necessary. If needed, tow it only to the nearest safe location so passengers can get off.

questions.question: If you may be running late, what should you do?

options.text: Drive faster.
Use flashing lights so others move out of your way.
Drive safely and arrive when you arrive.
Get upset.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive safely and arrive when you arrive.
questions.explanation: Do not drive dangerously or aggressively. Accept delays and stay calm. Plan for delays ahead of time to avoid stress.

questions.question: What are placards?

options.text: Warning signs on vehicles that show what dangerous cargo is inside.
A type of tire used in snowy conditions.
Logs kept inside the vehicle.
Journals for tracking mileage.

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning signs on vehicles that show what dangerous cargo is inside.
questions.explanation: Placards are diamond-shaped warning signs placed on vehicles carrying hazardous materials. They identify the type of hazard in the cargo.

questions.question: When you leave your vehicle, you should:

options.text: Apply the parking brake.
Apply the air brakes.
Not apply any brake.
Disconnect the trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: Apply the parking brake.
questions.explanation: Always apply the parking brake when leaving your vehicle.

questions.question: When checking the inside of a bus, you should:

options.text: Remove the emergency exit handles.
Assume all buzzers work properly.
Check that all seats are fastened securely.
Skip checking the handrails and floor.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check that all seats are fastened securely.
questions.explanation: Check that everything is safe and working properly. Make sure all seats are firmly fastened to the bus so riders are safe.
